column13:
Familiarity with Campus Stray & Pet Welfare at CIT-U
Measurement Scale: Standard 1 to 5-Point Likert Scale (1 = Never observed / Uninvolved, 5 = Highly involved / Active caretaker)
column14: PU1 (Sighting Reporting): The sighting submission form captures all critical details (photo, location landmark, physical state) needed to locate and rescue campus animals.
column15: PU2 (Directory Transparency): The system clearly differentiates between Permanent Campus Residents and Strays Available for Adoption, presenting vaccination badges and TNR status accurately.
column16: PU3 (Campus Biosecurity & Rabies Quarantine): The prominent active 14-day observation quarantine alerts for reported bite/scratch incidents provide critical safety protection for the CIT-U community in compliance with RA 9482.
column17: PU4 (Institutional Coordination): Task Force Bruno provides a significantly more structured, trackable coordination platform than unorganized Facebook groups or group chats.
column18: PU5 (Overall Campus Utility): Overall, the platform addresses real, urgent animal welfare and stray population management challenges across the CIT-U campus.
column19: PEOU1 (Navigation & Layout): The user interface hierarchy (navigation bars, cards, action buttons) is intuitive and easy to navigate without needing a user manual.
column20: PEOU2 (Form Efficiency): The input forms (sighting reports, adoption inquiries, profile views) are straightforward to complete with clear validation cues.
column21: PEOU3 (Visual Coherence & Aesthetics): The typography, official maroon/gold branding, responsive spacing, and SVG iconography feel clean, professional, and visually engaging.
column22: PEOU4 (Session Continuity): The system maintains an active session smoothly while working, without abrupt unexpected logouts during active typing or browsing.
column23: TECH1 (Collar QR Scanner): The hardware camera viewfinder and image file QR decoder resolved pet profiles quickly and accurately.
column24: TECH1-B (Public Emergency Pet Passport): Being able to scan an animal's collar and immediately view emergency medical information and security hotlines without forcing an immediate login is highly practical in emergencies.
column25: TECH2 (AI Trait & Keyword Search): The search accurately returned relevant animal profiles when searching with physical descriptors (e.g., "calico cat", "white socks") and handled exclusions appropriately.
column26: TECH3 (Multi-Device Responsiveness): The application adapted seamlessly between mobile phones and widescreen desktops without clipped cards, awkward overflows, or excessive dead white space.
column27: PERF1 (Responsiveness & Latency): The application loaded screens and submitted forms smoothly without frustrating delays or network timeouts.
column28: PERF2 (System Stability): The application operated reliably without unexpected crashes, broken links, stuck loaders, or unhandled database errors during my walkthrough.
column29: SUS-B1: I think that I would like to use Task Force Bruno frequently for campus animal welfare
column30: SUS-B2: I found the system unnecessarily complex or difficult to understand.
column31: SUS-B3: I felt very confident navigating and using the features of the system.
column32: SUS-B4: I needed to learn too many things or ask for help before I could use the system effectively.
column33: STF1 (Sighting Intake Handoff): The ability for staff to verify an animal sighting and directly admit it into pet registration (auto-filling location and photo) eliminates redundant manual data entry.
column34: STF2 (Supply Dimensional Clarity): Tracking inventory by genuine physical units (kilograms for kibble, cans for wet food, vials for vaccines, pieces for assets) provides clear and realistic supply management.
column35: STF3 (Collar Tag Generation): The integrated QR tag generator makes it easy for staff to create and print official, scannable collar tags for campus animals.
column36: SAT1 (Overall Satisfaction): Overall, how satisfied are you with your experience using Task Force Bruno?
column37: BI1 (Adoption Intention): Assuming full campus rollout at CIT-U, I intend to actively use Task Force Bruno whenever I encounter stray animals, resident companions, or adoption opportunities
column38: BI2 (Endorsement / Recommendation): I would enthusiastically recommend Task Force Bruno to fellow students, campus staff, and animal welfare advocates.
